previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of COPD and recurrent pneumonias, was admitted for respiratory distress, hypotension, and altered mental status. She was initially managed in the ICU with IV antibiotics, a norepinephrine drip, and a central line due to hypotension and severe hypoxia. Imaging confirmed right lower lobe pneumonia with possible pleural effusion. Her condition improved rapidly with nebulized treatments and antibiotics. She was weaned off vasopressors, transitioned to oral levofloxacin, and started on a prednisone taper. Anxiety was noted to exacerbate her dyspnea. She remained stable, was discharged home with service, and instructed to complete her antibiotic and steroid courses, continue home medications, and reduce her nicotine patch dose.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o woman with PMHx of T1-T2 paraplegia, COPD and recurrent 
PNAs who presents after recent discharge with respiratory 
distress and somnolence, concern for new RLL infiltrate.

# Respiratory Distress: Mixed hypoxic/hypercarbic resp failure. 
Pt with COPD and recurrent PNAs who developped tachypnea, 
increased O2 requirement, cough and lethargy acutely this 
morning. She was referred into the ED by her PCP and underwent ___ 
CTA that was negative for PE but revealed RLL consolidation, 
unclear if new or resolving from prior admission. Pt became 
increasingly somnolent in the ED with pCO2 in ___. In the ED she 
got steroids, alb/atrov and BIPAP, with improved mental status 
and minimal O2 requirement. Given increased WBC and possible 
consolidation and recent hospital admission, she was treated for 
HAP with cefepime and vancomycin. A PICC line was placed so that 
she could complete a 7-day course of antibiotics. There was 
concern of recurrent aspiration. Patient underwent a speech and 
swallow eval and passed. Her diet was restarted.  Her initial 
PICC placed at the bedside went up the right IJ, so it was 
removed and replaced by interventional radiology.  ___ she 
had hypotension and a low-grade fever to 100.7 at 1am.  She was 
given fluids and looked well clinically.  Her CXR was unchanged, 
U/A was negative and blood cultures had no growth at the time of 
discharge. Her vancomycin was originally dosed 1250mg Q24 hours, 
but a trough level was 3.8, so the dosing was changed to 1000mg 
Q12 hours for the remainder of the course.

# T1-T2 Paraplegia with chronic pain: pt is maintained on 
multiple sedating drugs for spasms and pain. She presented with 
respiratory distress and progressive somnolence and hypercarbia. 
Suspect a component of obesity hypoventilation with possible 
aspiration PNA. During this admission, her clonazpeam, 
pregabalin, and trazodone were initially held. Baclofen was 
decreased to 5 mg tid. Methadone and oxybutynin were continued 
at outpatient doses.  Her pregabalin and trazodone were added 
back on, but her Baclofen was continued at 5mg TID with some 
minor leg spasticity, but adequate pain control.  She was 
switched to Ultram for breakthrough pain, but did not find this 
effective, so she was switched back to Oxycodone.  She was 
discharged, finally, on the same doses of methadone and 
oxycodone, a reduced dose of baclofen, and off of Klonopin.  She 
was given 2 weeks of methadone and oxycodone to last until she 
can see Dr. ___ she was supposed to get refills the 
day of her admission but ended up being transferred to the ED.
.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Shortness of breath.

Comparison radiographs are available from ___ through ___.

UPRIGHT PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  
Patchy ground glass opacities at the lung bases and the left upper lobe are
redemonstrated.  In comparison to the prior radiograph from ___,
there is no significant change.  In comparison to multiple prior radiographs,
these opacities have appeared and resolved at different locations.  Moderate
cardiomegaly is unchanged.  The hilar mediastinal contours are stable.
Bilateral humeral cortical plates and screws demonstrate no evidence of
loosening.

IMPRESSION:  Transient pulmonary opacities over the past multiple radiographs
may be compatible with several entities, including chronic eosinophilic
pneumonia or aspiration.  Overall, the findings are not significantly changed
since ___ however, it is not known whether the underlying
pathology was improved or worse during the interval period as no intervening
radiograph demonstrating resolution is available. An underlying infectious
process cannot be excluded.

INDICATION:  Shortness of breath and hypoxia.

COMPARISON:  Radiographs available from ___ through ___
and CTA chest from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images of the chest were performed with and
without IV contrast.  Sagittal, coronal, and left and right oblique
reconstructions were performed for better evaluation of the pulmonary
vasculature.

CT OF THE CHEST WITH AND WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  
The bolus timing is suboptimal, resulting in decreased opacification of the
segmental and subsegmental pulmonary arteries. Within this limitation, there
is no evidence of pulmonary embolism within the main pulmonary arteries.  The
main pulmonary artery appears slightly enlarged, measuring 32 mm in diameter,
compared to 27 mm on the prior study from ___, but this apparent
increase is likely due to pulsation artifact.

Moderate-to-severe bibasilar atelectasis is seen, with significant volume loss
of the right lower lobe, with some consolidative features.  No effusion is
present.  Patchy air-space opacity also present within the lingula and left
upper lobe, increased compared to prior chest CT examination.  There is a
moderate degree of paraseptal emphysema.
An azygos lobe is redemonstrated.  There is no pneumothorax. Left calcified
hilar node is unchanged from prior.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  
There is no acute fracture or dislocation.  Multiple bilateral chronic rib
fractures are seen and unchanged.  

IMPRESSION:
1.  Assessment for pulmonary embolism within the segmental and subsegmental
pulmonary arterial branches is limited due to suboptimal bolus timing. No 
evidence of pulmonary embolism in the main pulmonary arteries.

2.  Moderate-to-severe bibasilar atelectasis, predominately within the right
lower lobe. A more consolidative element within the right lower lobe along
with a new lingular patchy opacity may reflect an infectious process.

3.  Paraseptal emphysema.

4.  Unchanged chronic rib cage deformities.

Findings discussed with Dr. ___ at 9:35 am, ___.

INDICATION:  Respiratory distress and possible right lower lobe pneumonia.

Comparison is made to the prior CTA of the chest of ___.

FINDINGS:  Right middle lobe consolidation,left upper and lower lobe
consolidative changes are unchanged.  Small right pleural effusion is
unchnaged.  Numerous bilateral rib fractures are unchanged.  The heart size is
mildly enlarged.  The remainder of the study is unchanged.

INDICATION:  Question aspiration.

COMPARISON:  None available.

SWALLOWING VIDEOFLUOROSCOPY:

Swallowing videofluoroscopy was performed in conjunction with the speech and
swallow division.  Multiple consistencies of barium were administered.  There
was penetration to straw sip thin liquids.  No aspiration was noted.

IMPRESSION:

Penetration to straw-sip thin liquids.

HISTORY:  PICC placement.

FINDINGS:  The PICC line extends into the right IJ system, out of view
superiorly.  It must be withdrawn at least 11-12 cm to be in the subclavian
vein.  This information was conveyed to ___, the IV nurse, by the resident
on call.

PICC LINE EXCHANGE/REPOSITIONING

INDICATION:  Malposition of indwelling PICC line.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, a guide wire was
advanced through the indwelling right arm PICC line, and subsequently into the
SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.  The old PICC line was then removed, and a
peel-away sheath was then placed over the guide wire. A new single lumen PICC
line measuring 47 cm in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath
with its tip positioned in the SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of
the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guide wire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated fluoroscopically guided PICC line exchange for a
new single lumen PICC line.  Final internal length is 47 cm, with the tip
positioned in the SVC.  The line is ready to use.

INDICATION:  Fever and hypotension.

Comparison is made to the prior study of ___.
